examples.solution_text:
Expand the square before multiplying each term by $-3$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-3(x-4)^2\\&=-3(x^2-8x+16)\\&=-3x^2+24x-48\end{aligned}$

Use the difference of two squares, then multiply each term by $-2$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-2(3x+4)(3x-4)\\&=-2\big((3x)^2-4^2\big)\\&=-2(9x^2-16)\\&=-18x^2+32\end{aligned}$

Keep the second expansion in brackets before changing every sign.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(x+7)^2-(x-7)^2\\&=x^2+14x+49-(x^2-14x+49)\\&=x^2+14x+49-x^2+14x-49\\&=28x\end{aligned}$
